data.name: FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION
data.detailed_description:
FINAL FANTASY XV: EPISODE ARDYN

For the first time, players take control of Noctis's greatest foe in this brand-new episode of FINAL FANTASY XV! Delve into the dark tale of scorned saviour Ardyn Lucis Caelum and unravel the secrets surrounding his mysterious past.

*Players must purchase FINAL FANTASY XV in order to access this content. Updating to the latest version of the game may also be required.


FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION MOD ORGANIZER


FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION MOD ORGANIZER is a tool to help you make mods for the FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION. It allows you to convert your assets into mod data and incorporate them into the game world.

The main function of MOD ORGANIZER is building model data and uploading mods to Steam Workshop. It does not have the functionality for creating and editing assets such as 3D models. Please create assets with your own tools and output them in FBX format, which MOD ORGANIZER can then import.

Your mods can be uploaded to Steam Workshop if you have a Steam account, and then shared with the community. Subscribe to Steam Workshop's mod data to use the mods in the Steam version of FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION.


Bonus: Half-Life Pack


Bonus: Half-Life Pack – Available now through the Workshop for all FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION owners on Steam!

  • Half-Life Costume (Main Game Exclusive)
    Protective gear made at the Black Mesa Research Facility.
  • Crowbar (Main Game Exclusive)
    Metallic tool that could prove quite useful in a pinch.
  • HEV Suit (COMRADES Exclusive)
    Full outfit for the entire body, exclusive to COMRADES. Protective suit made at the Black Mesa Research Facility.
  • Scientist Glasses (COMRADES Exclusive)
    Decorative accessory for the face, exclusive to COMRADES. Thick-rimmed black glasses that exude an air of quiet intelligence.
  • Crowbar (COMRADES Exclusive)
    Metallic tool that could prove quite useful in a pinch. Exclusive to COMRADES.


Playable Demo Out Now!

Get a sneak peek into how it all starts with the demo version of FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION.

*Spec may differ from the product version.

Take the journey, now in ultimate quality. Boasting a wealth of bonus content and supporting Native4K(3840×2160px) ultra high-resolution graphical options and HDR 10, you can now enjoy the beautiful and carefully-crafted experience of FINAL FANTASY XV like never before.

*The main difference to the product version is that sub-quests have been disabled.

  • The download size for the FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION PLAYABLE DEMO is 21GB. The High-Res 4K textures are included in this demo and are turned on or off automatically depending on your hardware specification.

  • In the final product, High-Res 4K textures will be an optional download and can be toggled on or off by the user.

The FINAL FANTASY XV WINDOWS EDITION PLAYABLE DEMO is a preview of the full game. We will continue to work on all aspects to ensure FFXV WINDOWS EDITION will be a great experience for PC gamers.


Reviews & Accolades

"A Must Have for RPG Fans!" - Gamezoom

"Final Fantasy XV: Windows Edition is the best version of the game." - Multiplayer it

"The attention to detail is astonishing" - Rock Paper Shotgun

"It looks stunning" - Tech Radar

"The ultimate way to play" - PC Invasion


FFXV WINDOWS EDITION 4K Resolution Pack


This pack allows you to enjoy FINAL FANTASY XV in high resolution.
Experience the world of FINAL FANTASY XV as you have never seen it before, with even more beautiful movie scenes and meticulously drawn characters and backgrounds.


Acerca do jogo


Get ready to be at the centre of the ultimate fantasy adventure, now for Windows PC.

Joined by your closest friends on the roadtrip of a lifetime through a breathtaking open world, witness stunning landscapes and encounter larger-than-life beasts on your journey to reclaim your homeland from an unimaginable foe.

In an action-packed battle system, channel the power of your ancestors to warp effortlessly through the air in thrilling combat, and together with your comrades, master the skills of weaponry, magic and team-based attacks.

Now realised with the power of cutting-edge technology for Windows PCs, including support for high-resolution displays and HDR10, the beautiful and carefully-crafted experience of FINAL FANTASY XV can be explored like never before.

KEY FEATURES:

Includes all of the exciting content released as part of continuous game updates (Chapter 13 alternate route, off-road Regalia customisation, character swap feature and more!). And comes with all of content released in the Season Pass - Episode Gladiolus, Episode Prompto, Multiplayer Expansion: Comrades, and Episode Ignis
Get ready to be at the centre of the ultimate fantasy adventure.

Main game:
  • FINAL FANTASY XV

New Features:
  • “Insomnia City Ruins: Expanded Map” – a new map that takes you right up to the end
  • First Person Mode
  • Armiger Unleashed
  • Use of the Royal Cruiser has been unlocked, with new fishing spots and recipes
  • Additional quest to acquire and upgrade the Regalia Type-D
  • Additional Achievements

DLC:
  • FFXV Episode Gladiolus
  • FFXV Episode Prompto
  • FFXV Episode Ignis
  • FFXV MULTIPLAYER EXPANSION: COMRADES
  • FFXV Booster Pack+
  • FFXV Holiday Pack+
*Moogle Chocobo Carnival tickets are not included in the FFXV Holiday Pack+.

Bonus Items:
  • [Weapon] Masamune (FFXV Original Model)
  • [Weapon] Mage Mashers (FFIX Model)
  • [Weapon] Blazefire Saber XV (FFXV Original Color)
  • [Weapon] Gae Bolg (FFXIV Model)
  • [Regalia Decal] Platinum Leviathan
  • [Regalia Decal] 16-Bit Buddies
  • [Regalia Decal] Cindymobile
  • [Regalia Decal] Gold Chocobo
  • [Outfit] Royal Raiment
  • [Item] Travel Pack

  • [Item] Angler Set
  • [Item] Gourmand Set

reviews.review:
This is my favorite game. Of all time, it's not close.

I would call Final Fantasy 15 a rushed, incomplete masterpiece. The game was in development hell for 10 years, so there's a bit of explanation that needs to be done why the game was rushed; from my understanding of events, the game started development as part of the Fabula Nova Crystallis series of games under the name Final Fantasy Versus 13. It underwent many design changes, had several engines created for it, with a scope that was ever-expanding but never within the realms of what could quite be done until eventually Square Enix finally said "Okay Nomura, it's been like 8 years we're putting Hajime Tabata on this, go make Kingdom Hearts again or something." Then, in the span of roughly 2 years, Hajime Tabata worked with Nomura to get a story that they'd be happy with, before using the assets at his disposal to rapidly rebuild and release the game, featuring a demo that had entirely unique story segments and mechanics that appeared nowhere in the final release and Episode Duscae which had different gameplay and UI elements. Also somewhere along the line they floated the idea of making it a musical allegedly, which is really funny.

Now, in the time they slapdashed a million assets together into a workable story and gameplay system, what did we get? Well, we got Final Fantasy 15 in all its glory; on its initial release, the pacing and plotline was a little confusing, with updates later adding cutscenes to the game to expand on what's going in its second half. 

The story follows Prince Noctis Lucis Caelum and his band of friends, including "contractually required to protect him" sworn shield Gladiolus Amicitia, "swore an oath to stay by his side forever" retainer Ignis Scientia, and "actual friend with no obligation outside of that" Prompto Argentum. These three characters will treat Noctis accordingly, because despite the fact they are all his friends, they all go about caring for him in their own ways. The 4 of them are the heart of the game, and their interactions with one another and Noctis are one of the most charming parts of the game. They have hundreds of lines of charming interactions for many situations. However, I want this review to be entirely spoiler free, so I'll leave it at that; but, I hate the complaint that the Episode DLCs were required to understand the story on launch. Nothing of note happens in Gladiolus's episode, Ignis's is fun and characterizes other characters in great ways but spoils the ending of the main plot for no reason, and Prompto's actually has important lore implications. Thankfully, the Windows Edition comes with all those DLCs, so you don't have to worry about that. There is supplementary material like this is a history class though, in the form of a short anime series, an anime OVA, an entire fucking movie, a mobile demake that doesn't work anymore and has exclusive dialogue, though none of these are required to understand the plot or what you're doing, or why you're doing it. They're good for understanding the world and politics at play in the game.

However, besides the story there's the combat; if I'm going to be honest, the combat is... it's somethin'. The combat is flashy, well animated, and rewards positioning and use of your allies, being able to command them to use special attacks, with the game actively rewarding you for using its mechanics with skill points. With proper positioning you can perform Link Strikes, where you and an ally will pull of a stylish combo move for pretty big damage on an opponent, often giving dialogue as you do so ("Noct, you're up!" "On it!"), or Blindside Attacks for bonus damage. Then there's warp strikes; your way of closing the distance, with damage that scales with the distance traveled. You can also select parts of enemies you want to attack, with breaking them often disabling or weakening parts of their moveset, or providing rewards. Different weapons are effective against different enemies, and some weapons have unique advantages to their moveset. The game's magic system is annoying, I genuinely dislike elemancy; the game's system in which you make magical grenades out of items you can find and elemental energy you can gather while roaming around, because it's both incredibly strong but also tedious to collect magical energy and figure out which one's gonna give "Decacast Firaza" and instantly nuke Behemoth, while also feeling lame because it doesn't feel like magic. All defensive options are bound to one button; it can dodge, it can parry, or roll when pressed. 90% of the game can be avoided using that button, and sure it uses MP to dodge for you, but MP can be recharged incredibly easily by warping to vantage points. You can cancel almost any weapon attack into a dodge if you press it right as it hits. Because of this, almost all combat devolves into holding the attack button until you notice an enemy trying to interrupt your combo. If mana gets low, you warp away and refill. Of course, I am oversimplifying, but the game's combat isn't that difficult, though it still has some complexities that make it fun.

The world is gorgeous and fun to explore. In every corner, there's things to find; ingredients to make new dishes to give you bonuses to your stats, shards to paint your car, and treasure spots. There is one glaring issue; the driving. It is almost entirely on rails and on-road for most of the game. The main mode of transport you will use offroad are very cute, have incredible music, and are fun.

Speaking of which, the music. This game's music is phenomenal, every track is genuinely incredible, Yoko Shimomura did incredible work. The boss theme fills you with awe and genuine fear because it opens with a choir, sounding genuinely menacing. Then it slips into a chant as the music gets more intense, allowing you to focus on the moment (Omnis Lacrima). The theme for doing the game's repeatable quests (Hunt or be Hunted) is just so beautifully tense. Yet, the combat themes are hardly the main selling point; Florence+The Machine's Stand By Me as the main theme is genuinely a fucking masterpiece, a powerful cover of an incredible song that was done ridiculously well. Some themes that play when exploring passively are so good I imagine them when walking around day to day; Sunset Waltz is a mainstay of my playlist for walks, Lestallum's theme perfectly encapsulates the charming urban atmosphere. The music is genuinely some of the best, it evokes all the emotions they're trying to.

What also evokes emotions are the things to do on the side; this game is full of side content you probably will not engage with. A pinball RPG game? Sure, whatever, go ahead! Want one of the most detailed and fun fishing games in a JRPG? Yup! Want to be a amateur photographer? Yeah, you can do that! Want to bet on monster gladiatorial combat? Fine, be my guest! Want to collect recipes and cook every meal to see who loves what? Don't bother, Cup Noodles are the ultimate flavor experience.

That's a joke you'll only if you play the fucking... this game has advertising, a ton actually. It fits in and never feels forced until Cup Noodles. Like all of the camping gear in game? That's a real brand, they were paid to put that in. Their outfits? Those are designer brands, those are real! They literally had a contractual obligation to put a wedding dress in a game but had nowhere to put it so they made a side quest to show it off to not violate the contract! I'm not joking, the amount of ad placement in this game is insane and I didn't notice any of it except the Cup Noodle one.

Every aspect of this game's development and fact I hear about is crazier than the last, and the fact this cobbled up mishmash worked into a storyline even a tenth cohesive and moving as it is, is a miracle.
